vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: gws-gmail-reply
Version: 1.0.7

The skill bundle provides documentation and instructions for an AI agent to use a CLI tool (gws) to reply to Gmail messages. The functionality described in SKILL.md is consistent with its stated purpose, covering standard email operations like threading, attachments, and HTML formatting without any indicators of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only wrapper that calls an existing gws CLI to send Gmail replies and its requirements (the gws binary) match its description, but it defers authentication and global flags to a separate shared SKILL.md you should inspect before use.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the SKILL.md: the skill simply invokes the 'gws' CLI to reply to Gmail messages. Requiring the 'gws' binary is proportionate and expected for this purpose; there are no unrelated binaries or credentials declared.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions are narrowly scoped to running the 'gws gmail +reply' command and list flags/behavior. However the SKILL.md explicitly points to ../gws-shared/SKILL.md for auth, global flags, and security rules — that external file is required for full runtime behavior, so you must review it because it likely contains authentication steps and additional policies the agent will follow.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files; this is instruction-only and so does not download or write code to disk. Lowest-risk install posture, assuming the 'gws' binary already present is legitimate.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: This skill declares no environment variables or credentials itself. That is consistent because it delegates auth to the shared gws-shared SKILL.md — but because auth is external, inspect gws-shared to confirm which credentials or tokens are actually required and ensure they are appropriate for a Gmail client (e.g., OAuth with limited scopes).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request persistent/system-wide changes. It does not attempt to modify other skills or agent configuration within its instructions.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: it runs the local 'gws' CLI to reply to Gmail messages. Before installing or using it, do the following: (1) Inspect ../gws-shared/SKILL.md (or run 'gws generate-skills' as instructed) to see exactly how authentication is performed and which credentials or OAuth scopes are required. (2) Verify the 'gws' binary on your system: confirm its origin, version, and that it is the official/expected tool (avoid running unknown binaries). (3) Test with --dry-run first to see the request the command will send. (4) If attachments are used, confirm where files are sourced from and that the gws tool does not upload them to unexpected endpoints. (5) If you cannot inspect gws-shared or the gws binary is untrusted, do not provide credentials or run the command.
